parts.title: Which Plant Dropped This Leaf? | Parts of a Leaf, Parallel vs Net Veins | P4 Science
parts.description:
A mystery leaf has landed on the buddies' Science Help Desk, and GLITCH the robot is sure it belongs to the mango tree. He has a scanner, a roll of sticky tape and a lot of confidence. Pick the clue that cracks the case: the colour, the size, or the parts of the leaf? Then follow Detective Basil as every suspect is cleared, one clue at a time.

In this video:
0:00 The case of the mystery leaf
0:36 Every case needs a witness
0:48 Pick a clue: 1, 2 or 3?
1:27 Clue 1: the colour
1:51 Clue 2: the size
2:33 Look closer: the parts of a leaf
3:01 Be a drop of water inside a leaf
3:37 The suspects: parallel or net veins?
4:59 GLITCH: show me the data
5:55 Did you spot the witness?
6:09 The words that earn marks
6:29 Case closed!
7:25 Blooper

Key words: leaf blade, leaf stalk, net veins, parallel veins.
The words that earn marks: The main parts of a leaf are the leaf blade, the leaf stalk, the main vein and the smaller veins. The leaf stalk attaches the leaf to the stem. The veins can be arranged in a parallel pattern or a net pattern.

For parents: children pick a clue with their fingers before each one is tested, then compare leaves part by part, side by side, like scientists. Primary 4 Science (Singapore Primary Science Syllabus 2023), Plant System: the parts of a leaf and how leaves differ. In the US, maple and oak leaves have net veins, while grass and corn have parallel veins. Also fits US NGSS 4-LS1-1 (Grade 4).
Try it: collect three fallen leaves on your way home. Hold each up to the light. Net veins or parallel veins? Straight edge or jagged edge?

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in and see whose score is highest at the end!
